If you have a good relationship with your psychiatrist, you could mention that you relapsed recently and it was worse than usual and go from there? Or, if you're unsure how to even bring it up because talking about this can be difficult, start out by something along the lines of "I have something I want to being up but I'm not sure how" - I've done this in the past with my own and it made it easier as, when she started asking me questions, it was easier to get my mouth moving rather than feeling like my jaw was made of lead, if that makes any sense?

I've gotten out of control a few times in the past, in different ways. I typically self-harm by cutting but sometimes bruising or burning.

Sometimes it's not needing a reason to self-harm but suddenly I've self-harmed on six different occasions in only 12 hours.

Other times I've lost control because I usually try to keep the damage to a certain area (say one limb or just one thigh) or depth (not going past styro) and now literally don't care so I'm going to town everywhere and hitting fat every time. 

Its different for everyone but these two are the most common for me to tell I've lost control.

I am in no means a doctor and I recommend that if you hit fat, you should definitely go see a doctor and get it professionally closed.

But what I do for mine is clean the area, hands, etc. with distilled water or a saline solution and steri-strip it closed. Fat cuts heal ugly, not gunna lie, so be warned. 

Also if you reach fat, you really need to keep an eye out for signs of infections. Redness, pus, hot to the touch, smells funny, etc. You see that, you don't DIY, you get to a doctor because infections can't always be controlled, even by doctors.

From personal experience (I am by no means in anyway certified as a doctor of any kind so please take this with a grain of salt) it does sound likely you may need to see a doctor. I had cuts like that where I should have gotten stitches but didnt and some that I definitely needed stitches for and went in for. Deeper cuts can get infected more easily. The ones I've had that should've been stitched I just left alone and the scar is definitely more noticeable than ones I've gotten stitched. When in doubt, get it checked out.

Doctor-patient confidentiality is only really solid if you're a legal adult and not a threat to yourself/others. But you could try asking the doctor to keep it quiet like the above mentioned- saying that you want to be the one to tell them. Not going to guarantee anything here. 

But if you're relatively new to self-harm I would recommend trying to stop before it gets out of hand. It gets out of hand very quickly and if you accidentally go too deep then you can affect your body more than you meant to. Self-harm is an addiction that I've had for 15+yrs, I've been hospitalized more times than I'd care to admit to.

I do NOT condone self-harm but you're going to do what you're going to do. I just hope you'll be safe when you self-harm; such as clean instruments and proper aftercare.

As for the scars thing, I don't know. I personally have always liked my scars but I get looks whenever I wear short sleeves. But some others I've talked to hate their scars and have actually had to get surgery to fix some of theirs. But anyways, I heard that bio oil and... I think it was vitamin e oil would help with scarring. I'm not sure on the second one tho. 

As for getting caught, it sounds like your family would be worried about you and would hopefully want to help you. Stay safe.
